narrationScript: For our second hands-on activity, your challenge is to extend our linked list implementation by creating a new function called `insert_at_end`. This function will take the current `head` of the list and an integer `value`, and its goal is to append a new node containing that value to the very end of the list. Here's a hint on the logic: First, you'll need to create your `new_node` and ensure its `next` pointer is set to `NULL`, as it will become the new last node. Next, consider an important edge case: what if the list is currently empty? If `head` is `NULL`, then your `new_node` simply becomes the new `head`. If the list is not empty, you'll need to **traverse** the list. Use a `current` pointer, starting from `head`, and keep moving `current` to `current->next` until `current->next` becomes `NULL`. At this point, `current` will be pointing to the *last* node in the original list. Finally, link this last node to your `new_node` by setting `current->next` to `new_node`. Remember, because the `head` of the list doesn't change when inserting at the end (unless the list was initially empty), you'll typically return the original `head` pointer.
